stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 5 x^{3} y + 20 x^{3} \). Decide whether it can be solved by separation of variables. If it can, write it with every factor involving y on the side of dy and every factor involving x on the side of dx; if it cannot, say so.

worked_solution.text: The two terms share the factor \( 5 x^{3} \), so \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 5 x^{3} y + 20 x^{3} = 5 x^{3}\left(y + 4\right) \), a function of x times a function of y.
worked_solution.rule_named: right side factored into a function of x times a function of y

worked_solution.text: Divide by \( y + 4 \) and multiply by dx: \( \frac{dy}{y + 4} = 5 x^{3}\,dx \).

options.label: \( \frac{dy}{y} = \left(5 x^{3} + 20 x^{3}\right)dx \)
options.derivation: only the first term divided by y, as though the sum split term by term

options.label: \( \left(y + 4\right)dy = 5 x^{3}\,dx \)
options.derivation: the factor y + 4 multiplied onto the dy side instead of divided

options.label: \( dy = 5 x^{3}\left(y + 4\right)\,dx \)
options.derivation: dx moved across with y still on the side of dx, so nothing was separated
